description: Start recording a narrated demo of the app you are building, from a DEMO INSTANCE on this machine (a second instance on a free port with a disposable data store; never the developer's own server or data). kind web: a 1440x900 Chromium at 2x on web.appUrl (sign in off camera with web.signIn steps or a storageState). kind electron: the app launched with scratch user data and HOME (electron.homeEnv names the app's own home-dir variables), or electron.attach to a build you started with a remote debugging port. kind terminal: a shell in a pseudo-terminal with a scratch HOME, filmed as a terminal window (terminal.setup runs off camera). kind ios: an iPhone app in the iOS Simulator (filmed upright; needs Xcode and AXe), at 2x points: ios.appPath installs its simulator build on a scratch simulator made for the take (ios.clone copies one of the developer's shut-down simulators, ios.udid films one as it is). ios.iphone films a real iPhone plugged into this Mac with a cable instead (the developer's own phone and data; the app already on it, or a device build in ios.appPath), upright or sideways as it is held when the take starts: Xcode signs a small helper app for it with the developer's team, and macOS asks once for Camera access to film its screen. kind android: an app on the Android emulator or a real phone or tablet, filmed at 2x dp upright or sideways as the device is held when the take starts (needs the Android SDK): android.apkPath installs its debug APK on a scratch emulator made for the take (android.avd boots one of the developer's AVDs read-only, android.serial films a running device as it is, a phone or tablet on USB included). kind screen (macOS): a native Mac app's own window, filmed and driven through its accessibility tree in the background (never the developer's pointer or keyboard), for what no page or device reaches; screen.foreground takes over the real screen instead, only with the developer's OK (screen.realScreenOk). Reads the features and docs sections from tday, records the git baseline, checks where the data lives, and swaps the developer's name, email, user name and machine name for a persona on screen. Needs ffmpeg. Read demo_guide and run demo_check first.

companions.description: Second screens filmed in lockstep with the take, in every beat, any number of them: each a terminal (not with kind terminal) or a browser window, uploaded as its own clip that tday lays out with the take. Each has a name (default its kind, then kind-2, ...). Their steps go in demo_beat's companionDo, each naming its companion; demo_beat's view and companionFocus say which one the film shows. The engine cannot see what a terminal's commands change, so with one the take's data needs store isolated or seeded, or liveLocalOk; a browser window's writes are guarded and counted like the take's.
